title: Soft-Body Masquerade Workshop
description: A soldier stands on a deformable coffeemat surface while the user sculpts and reshapes a soft-body venice_mask by applying directional forces, pinning vertices, and transferring elastic energy between the mask and the mat. The goal is to mold the mask onto the soldier's face through a sequence of coupled soft-body interactions with full undo/redo support.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 with GLTFLoader and OrbitControls from CDN. Load coffeemat.glb as a ground plane, venice_mask.glb floating at head height, and soldier.glb standing upright on the mat. Implement a spring-mass soft-body simulation for both the mask and the coffeemat surface: convert their meshes into particle grids connected by spring constraints. The mat has 20x20 resolution, the mask uses its vertex topology. Both obey a global energy conservation law: total elastic potential energy across both objects remains constant, so deforming one transfers stiffness energy to the other. Camera: perspective at (0,1.5,3) looking at origin. Lighting: warm directional light plus ambient. Interactions (10-14 steps required): 1) Click-drag on the mask to apply directional force vectors that deform it (soft pull/push). 2) Shift+click to pin/unpin mask vertices as anchor points. 3) Click-drag on the coffeemat to create indentations; energy removed from mat increases mask rigidity and vice versa. 4) Press F to toggle a wind force that ripples both soft bodies simultaneously. 5) Scroll wheel adjusts global damping coefficient affecting both bodies. 6) Press G to toggle gravity strength between 0.5x, 1x, 2x. 7) Press M to attempt fitting the mask onto the soldier's face using a lerp-to-target animation constrained by current softness. 8) Ctrl+Z for undo and Ctrl+Y for redo, storing full particle state snapshots (positions, velocities, pin states, energy distribution) in a history stack of up to 30 entries. Display a HUD showing total system energy, mask softness percentage, mat softness percentage, step count, and undo/redo stack depth. Use requestAnimationFrame with Verlet integration at 60fps. Color the mask vertices by local strain magnitude using a blue-to-red gradient. The coffeemat should show displacement via vertex color green channel intensity.
